payload.detail: CHARACTERISED AND PINNED, NOT FIXED, in PR #2860 (tests/clinical-safety.test.ts, 'safety finding precision'). Raised by the 2026-09-17 external audit (its finding C4). Its separate numeric-truncation claim is REFUTED and should not be re-checked: truncateAtSafeBoundary (clinical-safety.ts:77-88) drops a whole numeric token rather than cutting inside one, fixed twice since audit L111 and pinned by two committed tests. WHAT IS REAL: extractSafetyFindings labels a passage with safetyPatterns.find - the FIRST entry in a severity-ordered array whose regex matches - over tokens broad enough to appear in ordinary clinical prose. Now demonstrated by committed tests: 'Review the chart again in six weeks' is Monitoring; 'Avoid delay in transferring the patient' is Contraindication, the top severity, stop tone, danger colour; 'Monitor the full blood count weekly and avoid missing a sample' is Contraindication because avoid sits earlier in the array than monitor. THE FALSE NEGATIVE IS THE MORE DANGEROUS DIRECTION and was uncovered: no pattern knows cease, withhold, hold the dose, boxed warning, black box, hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis, so a passage whose entire content is a stop instruction produces NO finding. FOUND WHILE WRITING THOSE TESTS, and not in the audit: every red-flag token is wrapped in word boundaries, so 'immediate' matches 'with immediate effect' and does NOT match 'immediately', the commoner clinical phrasing. That is a plain regex defect, not the first-match-wins mechanism, and it has its own pinned case. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED: answerSupportPriority (src/components/clinical-dashboard/evidence-panels.tsx:139-147) promotes the most severe safety finding AHEAD OF EVERYTHING ELSE as the answer's headline support card, so changing which passages carry a label changes what a clinician sees first. That is an owner decision about clinical display, not a defect to fix in passing. NEXT: decide the vocabulary (the adverb-form defect is the cheapest and least contentious part), and decide separately whether a regex-derived finding should hold the headline position at all. When the labels change, update the characterisation tests and move their reasoning with them - a green run there is not evidence the labels are clinically right. PARTLY FIXED 2026-09-18, owner-approved. The vocabulary half landed: cease/ceasing/ceased, withhold, hold-the-dose (phrase-bounded), boxed warning, black box, anaphylaxis now match at red_flag, and 'known hypersensitivity'/'hypersensitivity to' at contraindication while a bare hypersensitivity stays at red_flag. The adverb defect is fixed - immediate(?:ly)? - so 'Seek help immediately.' is a finding instead of nothing. Stop instructions went to red_flag rather than contraindication deliberately: a stop instruction is event-driven while a contraindication is a standing property of the patient, both carry the stop tone, and keeping them one tier down means NO passage that reads Contraindication or Red flag today changes label. The only label movement is Monitoring -> Red flag, plus (none) -> a finding. Verified: 32/32 in tests/clinical-safety.test.ts, and 124/124 across the five other suites that touch safety findings. One accepted false positive is pinned by its own test: 'The tremor ceased overnight.' is now a Red flag - loud rather than silent, which is the trade. STILL OPEN, and the reason this row stays open: whether a regex-derived finding should hold the headline support position at all (answerSupportPriority promotes the most severe finding ahead of everything else). That is recorded as the SAFETY-CHIP-VOCABULARY open assurance decision in docs/clinical-hazard-controls.json, visible in the developer hub. ALSO FOUND: the same word-boundary defect makes 'escalat' and 'monitor' match nothing - raised separately, not fixed here, because both move labels and need the same sign-off.
